title: It just won't come on
setting: A weekday evening. Yuki gets home from work to a dark living room. Her little brother Kenji is in there, playing a video game by the light of the TV.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.kana: え、くらい！けんじ、いるの？
lines.english: Huh, it's dark! Kenji, are you home?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nande denki tsukenaide geemu shiteru no?
lines.ja: なんで電気つけないでゲームしてるの？
lines.kana: なんででんきつけないでげーむしてるの？
lines.english: Why are you playing games without putting the light on?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: denki, tsukenai n ja nakute, tsukanai n da yo.
lines.ja: 電気、つけないんじゃなくて、つかないんだよ。
lines.kana: でんき、つけないんじゃなくて、つかないんだよ。
lines.english: It's not that I'm not putting the light on. It won't come on.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: え、つかないの？リモコンは？
lines.kana: え、つかないの？りもこんは？
lines.english: What, it won't come on? What about the remote?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: kore. botan, nando mo oshita kedo, dame.
lines.ja: これ。ボタン、何度も押したけど、だめ。
lines.kana: これ。ぼたん、なんどもおしたけど、だめ。
lines.english: Here. I've pressed the button over and over. Nothing.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto da. botan oshite mo, denki tsukanai. denchi kana?
lines.ja: ほんとだ。ボタン押しても、電気つかない。電池かな？
lines.kana: ほんとだ。ぼたんおしても、でんきつかない。でんちかな？
lines.english: You're right. I press the button and the light doesn't come on. The batteries, maybe?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.kana: でんちはきのうかえたよ。

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, nande darou. a! kinou no yoru, denki keshita no, kenji?
lines.ja: じゃあ、なんでだろう。あ！昨日の夜、電気消したの、ケンジ？
lines.kana: じゃあ、なんでだろう。あ！きのうのよる、でんきけしたの、けんじ？
lines.english: Then why...? Oh! Kenji, was it you who turned the light off last night?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. asoko no suitchi de keshita.
lines.ja: うん。あそこのスイッチで消した。
lines.kana: うん。あそこのすいっちでけした。
lines.english: Yeah. I turned it off at the switch over there.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore da yo! suitchi de denki keshitara, rimokon no botan oshite mo tsukanai no.
lines.ja: それだよ！スイッチで電気消したら、リモコンのボタン押してもつかないの。
lines.kana: それだよ！すいっちででんきけしたら、りもこんのぼたんおしてもつかないの。
lines.english: That's it! If you turn the light off at the switch, it won't come on however much you press the remote.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou. jaa, asoko no suitchi de tsukete mite.
lines.ja: そう。じゃあ、あそこのスイッチでつけてみて。
lines.kana: そう。じゃあ、あそこのすいっちでつけてみて。
lines.english: Yep. Go on, try putting it on with that switch over there.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: desho? ato, kenji no heya, denki tsuiteru yo.
lines.ja: でしょ？あと、ケンジの部屋、電気ついてるよ。
lines.kana: でしょ？あと、けんじのへや、でんきついてるよ。
lines.english: Told you. Oh, and the light's on in your room.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ee. keshite kite. kaaten mo shimetoite.
lines.ja: えー。消してきて。カーテンも閉めといて。
lines.kana: えー。けしてきて。かーてんもしめといて。
lines.english: Ugh. Go turn it off for me. And shut the curtains while you're there.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jibun de yatte! denki wa rimokon de keshite ne!
lines.ja: 自分でやって！電気はリモコンで消してね！
lines.kana: じぶんでやって！でんきはりもこんでけしてね！
lines.english: Do it yourself! And use the remote to turn the light off!

choices.english: The remote's batteries were dead, so Yuki put new ones in and the light came on.
The light wouldn't come on from the remote because Kenji had turned it off at the wall switch last night. Turning it on at the switch fixed it.
Kenji was playing in the dark on purpose, so Yuki turned the light on at the switch herself.

questions.explanation: Lines 4-7: the light won't come on (tsukanai), however often Kenji and then Yuki press the remote's button. Lines 9-11: Kenji turned it off at the switch last night (suitchi de keshita), and once that happens the remote can't turn it back on. Lines 13-14: Kenji turns it on at the switch and it comes on (a, tsuita!). A is wrong: Kenji changed the batteries yesterday (line 8: denchi wa kinou kaeta yo), so they weren't the problem. C is wrong: Kenji wasn't choosing the dark (line 4: tsukenai n ja nakute, tsukanai). Also, Kenji turns it on at the switch, not Yuki.

questions.english: You walk into a room with Yuki in the evening, and she says, "kono heya, kurai ne." (This room's dark, isn't it?) Offer to put the light on.
questions.answer: Offer with denki and tsukeru in its 'shall I?' form: un, denki tsukeyou ka?

modelAnswers.english: Yeah. Shall I put the light on?
I'll put the light on, then.

questions.explanation: A light goes on with tsukeru. Yuki asks why Kenji is playing with the light off (line 3: nande denki tsukenaide...?) and later tells him asoko no suitchi de tsukete mite (line 13). tsukeyou ka? offers to do it, and tsukeru ne says you're doing it now. Don't carry akeru (open) over from doors, and don't say denki o ireru: ireru goes with suitchi (switch) or dengen (power), not with the light itself.

questions.english: Yuki suddenly guesses what went wrong. What does she ask Kenji?
questions.ja: ユキさんはケンジさんに何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはけんじさんになんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa kenji-san ni nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: Did you shut the light last night, Kenji? (shimeru, the door verb)
choices.romaji: kinou no yoru, denki shimeta no, kenji?

choices.english: Did you cut off the power last night, Kenji?
choices.romaji: kinou no yoru, denki tometa no, kenji?

choices.english: Was it you who turned the light off last night, Kenji?
choices.romaji: kinou no yoru, denki keshita no, kenji?

questions.explanation: Line 9: kinou no yoru, denki keshita no, kenji? A light goes off with kesu, and Kenji answers with the same verb in line 10 (suitchi de keshita). A is 'shut' put into Japanese: shimeru is for doors, windows and curtains. Kenji uses it for the curtains in line 16 (kaaten mo shimetoite), right after keshite kite for his light. B, denki o tomeru, means cutting off the power supply (what happens when the bill isn't paid), not switching off a light.

questions.english: Yuki asks Kenji why he's playing games without putting the light on. From his answer, why is the room dark?
questions.ja: 部屋はなんで暗いんですか？
questions.kana: へやはなんでくらいんですか？
questions.romaji: heya wa nande kurai n desu ka?

choices.english: Kenji has tried to put it on, but the light won't come on.
Kenji likes playing games in the dark, so he's left the light off.
Kenji forgot to put the light on because he was busy with his game.

questions.explanation: Line 4: denki, tsukenai n ja nakute, tsukanai n da yo. tsukenai (from tsukeru) is a person not putting it on, which is what Yuki assumed in line 3. tsukanai (from tsuku) is the light itself not coming on, and that is what's happening: he has pressed the remote's button over and over (line 6). The light takes tsuku all through the scene: tsuita when it finally comes on (line 14) and tsuiteru for the one left on in his room (line 15). B and C are both the tsukenai that Kenji denies: it isn't that he chose not to, or forgot. He tried and it won't work.

questions.english: Yuki hands you the light's remote and says, "kore de denki tsukete." (Put the light on with this.) It has lots of buttons. Ask her which one to press.
questions.answer: Ask which button with dono botan and osu: dono botan osu no?

modelAnswers.ja: どのボタンを押せばいい？

questions.explanation: You press a button with osu. Kenji says botan, nando mo oshita kedo (line 6), Yuki says botan oshite mo, denki tsukanai (line 7), and in line 11 she says rimokon no botan oshite mo tsukanai no. Casual speech drops the o (botan osu no?). Pressing the button is osu; what the light does is tsuku, and what you do to it is tsukeru. The same botan o osu works for lifts, the stop button on a bus and ticket machines.

newWords.english: remote control (here, for the ceiling light)
switch (here, the light switch on the wall)
stop; denki o tomeru = cut off the power supply (only in a quiz choice)
